question:
(i) Explain the quantisation of electric charge and write its mathematical expression.
(ii) A body has charge $-9.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$. Find the number of excess electrons on it. Take $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.

options.A:
(i) Charge is continuous and can have any fractional value of $e$
(ii) The body has 9.6 excess electrons
options.B:
(i) $q=\frac{e}{n}$ where $n$ is a fraction
(ii) The body has 3 excess electrons
options.C:
(i) Quantisation means $q=ne$, where $n$ is an integer and $e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$
(ii) $\frac{9.6\times10^{-19}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}=6$ excess electrons
options.D:
(i) $q=ne^2$ where $n$ is always positive
(ii) The body has 6 deficient electrons
